D1 research authoring, batch 83 (2026-09-27): two ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1 and 2 (phantom-limb-pain, amputation-or-loss-of-use) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. Rank 1 is the strongest level-specific quantitative finding located in this batch; rank 2 is a DEFINITIONAL AND DOCUMENTARY relationship carrying the lowest interpretive weight and is disclosed as resting on catalog structure rather than on evidence.

Classification guard: both edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true). The rank 1 edge is at NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION, following the existing registry precedent for this target which already carries that category on two incoming edges, and its vector names cortical reorganisation as a CANDIDATE rather than a demonstrated mechanism, since the located survey reports an epidemiological level-gradient without testing the mechanism. The rank 2 edge is at POST_SURGICAL_OR_TREATMENT because the relationship originates in a surgical act, and its causation status states that the loss-of-use determination is FUNCTIONAL AND CASE BY CASE rather than a medical consequence, and that no located biological vector describes it. Both edges note the located survey's 31-YEAR MEAN TIME SINCE AMPUTATION, so neither is applied to an early postoperative claimant.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: no complex-regional-pain-syndrome edge (DIRECTION REVERSAL - the target identity has ZERO registered incoming edges, but the located complex-regional-pain literature addresses amputation PERFORMED AS A TREATMENT for intractable pain, with a case series of long-term outcomes of amputation in the treatment of complex regional pain syndrome and a decision-making analysis for amputation for complex regional pain syndrome type I, which is the OPPOSITE direction from the one this edge name would imply, so it is refused rather than authored inverted; this is recorded here as a named candidate for a future batch, since amputation as a treatment for an established pain condition is a real relationship that would need its own direction-disclosed edge); no residual-limb-pain edge (MISSING IDENTITY, the catalog carries no residual-limb-pain identity despite a pooled prevalence of 58 percent in the located systematic review, and the neuroma identity is likewise absent, which together are the most significant catalog gaps this batch surfaced); no depressive-disorder or anxiety-disorder edge (CHAIN-CONFLICT, since phantom-limb-pain already carries edges to both and the amputation-or-loss-of-use identity carries one to depressive-disorder, so authoring either from this file would duplicate relationships the graph already resolves); and no spinal-cord-injury or brachial-plexus edge (SCOPE, recorded as a named candidate, since a shoulder disarticulation is frequently performed for brachial plexus avulsion or for a non-viable limb after plexus injury and that indication is a separate documented condition).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: This is the strongest quantitative file in the batch because a national veteran survey reports a shoulder-level-specific effect: a national survey of 776 US military veterans with major upper limb amputation found that 73 percent reported phantom limb pain with a mean intensity of 4.2 (SD 3.4), that 42 percent reported it daily to always, and critically that AMPUTATION AT THE SHOULDER WAS ASSOCIATED WITH ANY PHANTOM LIMB PAIN AT AN ODDS RATIO OF 3.78 (95 percent CI 1.93 to 7.39), with amputation at the transhumeral level at 1.76 (1.10 to 2.81) and amputation due to cancer at 5.33 (1.15 to 24.81), and that AMPUTATION AT THE SHOULDER LEVEL WAS ASSOCIATED WITH A 1.5-POINT HIGHER AVERAGE PAIN INTENSITY SCORE (P<0.001) COMPARED WITH THE TRANSRADIAL LEVEL (PMID 32896094); a nationwide cross-sectional survey of 3,374 unilateral upper and lower limb amputees found that clinical and demographic variables including age at and level of amputation explained 10.6 percent of the variance in phantom limb pain while perceptual variables explained 16.9 percent, and that these variables were SPECIFIC FOR PHANTOM LIMB PAIN AND NOT FOR RESIDUAL LIMB PAIN, pointing at partly different mechanisms (PMID 34583023); and a systematic review and meta-analysis of upper extremity amputation found a pooled residual limb pain prevalence of 58 percent (95 percent CI 46 to 68) and symptomatic neuromas at 22 percent (95 percent CI 11 to 33) (PMID 40439077); recorded as documented association only, with the shoulder-specific odds ratio registered as the anchor that makes this identity distinct rather than another amputation level.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence is a cross-sectional association in a population that self-selected into a specific military amputation programme: the veteran survey is cross-sectional, so it establishes that shoulder-level amputation is associated with phantom limb pain in this cohort rather than that it produces it, and its respondents were 97 percent male with a mean age of 63 years and a MEAN TIME SINCE AMPUTATION OF 31 YEARS, meaning the finding describes a very long-term survivor population and not the early postoperative period a claimant may be describing. Its shoulder-level odds ratio of 3.78 carries a confidence interval of 1.93 to 7.39, which is wide, and the cancer-amputation estimate of 5.33 carries an interval of 1.15 to 24.81, which spans more than an order of magnitude. The nationwide survey explains only about 11 percent of the variance in phantom limb pain from clinical and demographic variables, so even the located predictors jointly account for a small share of the outcome and no located anchor supplies a mechanism by which a shoulder-level amputation produces a larger phantom pain field. Individual claims require a dated shoulder disarticulation or shoulder-level amputation with the level and aetiology documented, a dated pain assessment with intensity and temporal course recorded, and exclusion of residual limb pain, neuroma, and stump infection as alternative sources of pain after the same surgery.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is cortical reorganisation after loss of the limb's sensory representation, in which the deafferented primary somatosensory cortex reorganises and adjacent facial and trunk representations expand into the vacated cortical territory, so that a more proximal amputation removes a larger volume of sensory cortex and leaves a larger cortical territory available for remapping, which is the located rationale for why shoulder-level amputation carries a higher odds ratio and a higher pain intensity than a distal transradial amputation; the mechanism is classified NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION to follow the existing registry precedent on this target, which already carries that category on two incoming edges, and the vector is offered as a candidate explanation for a documented epidemiological gradient rather than as a demonstrated mechanism, since the located survey reports the gradient without testing the mechanism.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at national-veteran-survey, nationwide-cross-sectional-survey, and systematic-review-meta-analysis class, following the file's existing biomechanical, post-injury, orthopedic, and treatment-related pathway scope: the veteran survey is the anchor that supplies the shoulder-SPECIFIC odds ratio of 3.78 and the 1.5-point intensity difference against transradial, which is the located evidence that makes shoulder disarticulation a distinct risk context rather than another amputation level, and it is registered together with its 31-year mean time since amputation and its wide confidence intervals (PMID 32896094); the nationwide survey is the anchor that quantifies the variance explained by amputation level and age and establishes that the predictors of phantom limb pain are SPECIFIC and distinct from those of residual limb pain (PMID 34583023); and the systematic review is the anchor for the pooled residual-limb-pain and neuroma prevalence, which is the located evidence for the residual-limb alternative that must be excluded (PMID 40439077). Because the relationship is a long-term cross-sectional association rather than a demonstrated mechanism, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names cortical reorganisation as a candidate rather than a demonstrated route, and requires the amputation level, aetiology, and pain course to be documented separately.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor is a CROSS-SECTIONAL survey of 776 veterans with a mean time since amputation of 31 YEARS, so it describes a long-term survivor population and cannot support attribution for an early postoperative claimant, and it is a single military programme's population, 97 percent male with a mean age of 63, which is not representative of all claimants; its shoulder-level estimate of 3.78 carries a confidence interval of 1.93 to 7.39 and its cancer-amputation estimate carries an interval spanning 1.15 to 24.81; the nationwide survey is also cross-sectional, covers unilateral amputees of both upper and lower limb, and explains only about 11 percent of the variance in phantom limb pain from clinical and demographic variables, so the located predictors jointly account for a small share of the outcome; the systematic review pools prevalence figures for RESIDUAL LIMB PAIN and neuromas, which are the principal alternative pain sources after the same surgery, so it functions as the exclusion anchor rather than as support for phantom pain; and NO located anchor supplies a mechanism test for the level-of-amputation gradient, so cortical reorganisation remains a candidate explanation. Two of the three references, the veteran survey and the nationwide survey, were ALREADY registered source entities before this batch and are reused as additional reference uses rather than duplicated.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Residual limb pain and symptomatic neuroma at the stump, pooled at 58 percent and 22 percent respectively after upper extremity amputation, which is the principal competing explanation for pain at the same surgical site
Stump or socket infection, which is documented as associated with persistent residual limb pain and would produce a different pain time course
Neurpathic pain from nerve injury at the disarticulation site, which is a different entity from referred phantom pain
Central pain or thalamic-level involvement, and pain attributable to a pre-existing condition present before the amputation

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the located national veteran survey reports a shoulder-SPECIFIC odds ratio of 3.78 for phantom limb pain and a 1.5-point higher mean intensity than transradial amputation, which is the strongest level-specific evidence in this batch and is directly relevant to a shoulder-disarticulation claim. The conservative framing records the 31-year mean time since amputation so the finding is not applied to an early postoperative claimant, reports the wide confidence intervals, names the pooled residual-limb-pain prevalence as the competing explanation, and states that cortical reorganisation is a candidate rather than a demonstrated mechanism.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: A shoulder disarticulation is an amputation and is documented under the registry's broad amputation or loss-of-use identity, which is a definitional co-occurrence rather than a causal progression and is recorded as such: this file's identity denotes a proximal upper-limb amputation, while the target identity denotes amputation or loss of use of limbs or digits as a rating construct, and the registry already carries five incoming edges to the target from vascular and neuropathic primaries (peripheral aneurysm, peripheral vascular disease, fasciitis, thromboangiitis obliterans, and Charcot arthropathy) together with one outgoing edge to depressive-disorder (PMID 32896094 anchors the level-specific amputation findings registered at this file's rank 1 edge, and the target identity's own registered edges are the located context for this definitional relationship). The edge is registered because a shoulder-disarticulation claim in a benefits record is documented under the amputation identity, and because a veteran whose record carries only a level-specific disarticulation label has not thereby had the general amputation claim characterised; the mechanism is named as the surgical act of disarticulation rather than as a disease process.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: No causal claim is made or available here, and the causation status disclaims the progression reading explicitly: this edge records a DEFINITIONAL AND DOCUMENTARY RELATIONSHIP between a specific amputation level and the broad amputation or loss-of-use rating identity, and it does not assert that a shoulder disarticulation produces a loss of use, which is a functional determination made case by case rather than a medical consequence of the procedure. The reading is also bidirectional in practice, since a loss-of-use claim for a shoulder may be documented under the amputation identity and an amputation claim may be characterised by level, so the edge expresses a documentation relationship rather than a clinical one. The located evidence assembled for this file does not itself support a definitional edge, because definitional relationships are established by the catalog rather than by citation, and the single reference registered on this edge is the level-specific amputation survey that documents the amputation population and its level distribution rather than any rating construct. Individual claims require a dated operative record documenting the disarticulation level and date, a dated functional assessment characterising loss of use, and separate documentation of the amputation and the functional claim.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is the SURGICAL ACT of disarticulation itself, through which the upper limb is separated at the shoulder joint and the limb and its distal musculature are removed, so that the loss of the limb is a direct and intended result of the operation rather than a downstream consequence of disease; the vector is named as the surgical act because that is what the edge actually records, and it is classified POST_SURGICAL_OR_TREATMENT because the relationship originates in a procedure rather than in a pathophysiology, while the loss-of-use determination itself is a functional and administrative construct that no located biological vector describes.

The conservative standard holds the edge at association only, states in the causation status that no causal claim is available and that the loss-of-use determination is functional and case-by-case, and discloses that the single registered reference supports the amputation population rather than any rating construct, since definitional relationships are established by the catalog and not by citation.
